mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has improved for three of the last four weeks (-33.4 to -25.4), indicating a steady return of commuting-linked trips that generates incidental retail stops, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -33.4 to -25.4 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days is not higher than prior 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing its upward trajectory.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT weekly mean crosses above -45 (less negative), it signals a meaningful recovery in transit ridership that enables broader errand and retail trips, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks of the crossing.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean rises above -45 for at least one week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT t-0w value is -43.6, above the -45 threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks after TRANSIT crosses above -45, or declines further despite the crossing.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous improvement in WORKPLACES and decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility jointly indicate a behavioral shift away from home-centric routines; their combined momentum compounds to drive RETAIL_REC upward faster than either series alone would predict.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises and RESIDENTIAL falls concurrently for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 14.9 to 9.4 while WORKPLACES rose from -33.4 to -25.4
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth rate over next 4 weeks is not greater than the growth rate implied by WORKPLACES alone, despite the joint RESIDENTIAL decline.

mechanism_narrative: The large PARKS spike at t-2w (43.0) followed by reversion toward baseline (17.3, 20.9) reflects a transient weekend/seasonal leisure effect that substitutes for retail trips; as PARKS stabilizes at elevated but non-spiking levels, substitution pressure eases and RETAIL_REC resumes its rise within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean falls back within 10 points of its 4-week average after a spike
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS spiked to 43.0 at t-2w then reverted to 17.3 and 20.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following PARKS reversion, or PARKS spikes again without RETAIL_REC recovery.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility oscillating in a narrow negative band (-22.3 to -15.6) without a clear worsening trend indicates no new essential-only restrictions are being imposed; this policy stability permits continued gradual reopening of non-essential retail, sustaining RETAIL_REC's upward trend.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM ranged narrowly between -22.6 and -15.6 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines even though GROCERY_PHARM remains range-bound, indicating the policy-stability mechanism does not hold.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week WORKPLACES increase exceeding 8 points (as seen from t-1w to t-0w: -35.3 to -25.4) signals an abrupt reopening of businesses that triggers a surge in retail visits within the next two weeks due to pent-up commuting-linked shopping demand.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose 9.9 points from t-1w (-35.3) to t-0w (-25.4)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to accelerate upward within two weeks of a WORKPLACES jump exceeding 8 points.

mechanism_narrative: Persistently elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility relative to pre-pandemic baseline, even while declining, indicates lingering risk-averse behavior; in a regime where RESIDENTIAL remains above 8 points, households continue to substitute delivery/local errands for discretionary retail trips, capping RETAIL_REC growth or reversing it.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean remains above 8 points
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL still at 9.4 at t-0w despite declining trend
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next 4 weeks even while RESIDENTIAL stays above 8 points, falsifying the risk-aversion cap mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime where PARKS mobility is structurally elevated (consistently positive, above 15 points for four straight weeks) due to early-summer seasonal outdoor preference, this sustained outdoor-activity baseline interacts with improving TRANSIT to indicate broader mobility normalization, jointly lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks beyond what either series predicts alone.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains above 15 points and TRANSIT improves week-on-week simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS stayed above 15 for all four weeks while TRANSIT improved from -51.0 to -43.6
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise, or rises no more than predicted by TRANSIT alone, despite sustained elevated PARKS and improving TRANSIT.
